body.p: The Office Action dated January 17, 2024, is received and carefully noted. Claims 1, 6, and 8-9 are amended. Support for the amendments may be found throughout the specification, for example, in Figure 3 and paragraphs [0034] and [0035] of the specification. Entry of the amendments at this time is proper as the amendments place the application in condition for allowance or reduce the number of issues for appeal. Claims 1 and 6-9 are pending in the present application and respectfully submitted for reconsideration in view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks.

Claims 1 and 6-9 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Fujiwara (Japanese Patent Publication No. 2016-214491) in view of Mitsukura (WIPO Publication No. 2018221750 ), Sakamoto (WIPO Publication No. 2009150765), Kogure (WIPO Publication No. 2019107012), and Cai (WIPO Publication No. 2020047750). Applicants respectfully traverse the obviousness rejection. The cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose or suggest the limitations of the pending claims.

Claims 1, 8, and 9 are the independent claims. Claim 1 recites "instantaneously generating a feature vector including a plurality of heart rate intervals that are consecutive in the sleeping period, wherein the feature vector is a variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector formed as a time series of a group of pieces of the normal RRI data having normal values respectively indicating the plurality of heart rate intervals in an identification target period having a fixed period length of about 60 seconds." Claim 1 also recites "inputting the variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector formed as the time series of the group of pieces of the normal RRI data as the feature vector to the processing unit operating as a recurrent neural network trained through machine learning in advance so as to output, in response to the variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector having been inputted, a value indicating a sleep state in the identification target period." Claims 8 and 9 recite similar
limitations. Applicants submit that the cited references fail to disclose or suggest these limitations of the independent claims.

With regard to Fujiwara, the Office Action, on page 8, lines 5-18, acknowledges that the cited reference does not teach "instantaneously generating a feature vector including a plurality of heart rate interval[s] that are consecutive in the sleeping period, wherein the feature vector is [a] vector formed as a time series of a group of pieces of the normal RRI data having normal values respectively indicating the plurality of heart rate intervals in an identification target period having a fixed length period of about 60 seconds." The Office Action also acknowledges that Fujiwara also does not teach "inputting the various length vector formed as the time series of the group of pieces of the normal RRI data as the feature vector to the processing unit operating as a recurrent neural network trained through machine learning in advance so as to output, in response to the feature vector having been inputted, a value indicating a sleep state in the identification target period." Thus, Fujiwara fails to disclose or suggest these features of the amended claims.

With regard to Mitsukura, this reference is not cited as teaching a variable length vector in a fixed period length. Thus, Applicants submit that Mitsukura cannot be held to disclose or suggest a variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector in an identification target period having a fixed period length, as recited in claims 1, 8, and 9. The combination of Fujiwara and Mitsukura fails to disclose or suggest these limitations of the amended claims.

With regard to Sakamoto, this reference is cited as teaching an identification target period as having a fixed period length. Sakamoto is not applied against the claims as disclosing or suggesting that the feature vector is a variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector indicating the plurality of heart rate intervals in the identification target period having a fixed period length. Thus, Sakamoto fails to disclose or suggest the limitations of claims 1, 8, and 9 missing from Fujiwara and Mitsukura.
With regard to Kogure, Applicants submit that this reference is not applied against the claims as teaching any of the features cited above. Thus, Kogure also fails to disclose or suggest the
limitations of claims 1, 8, and 9 missing from Fujiwara and Mitsukura.

The Office Action cites Cai as teaching these limitations of claims 1, 8, and 9 cited above. The Office Action states that it would have been obvious "to modify the invention of Fuji to include inputting variable length feature vectors into the recurrent neural network of Cai in order for detecting an arrhythmia." Applicants respectfully submit that Cai fails to disclose or suggest the limitations of claims 1, 8, and 9 missing from Fujiwara, Mitsukura, Sakamoto, and Kogure.

As noted by the Office Action, Cai describes "the recurrent neural network, based on the characteristics of the recurrent neural network, [ ]can detect ECG signals of different lengths," on page 3. Cai describes, based on ECG signals of different lengths, features in the ECG signals are automatically extracted and integrated, as stated on page 9. Thus, Cai teaches a variable-length ECG signal.

Cai fails to disclose or suggest a variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector in an identification target period having a fixed period length. Instead, Cai describes a variable-length signal that has a different length of period, or a different length of time. Cai does not disclose or suggest a different number of elements, or the number of normal RRI data, of a vector in a fixed period length.

Referring to Figure 3 of the present application, shown below, it may be appreciated that the number of RRIs measured in the identification target period, which is a fixed period, is not a constant number. Thus, the number of elements of the variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector is variable.

The period length, however, is fixed. Cai fails to disclose or suggest these limitations of claims 1, 8, and 9. Further, one skilled in the art would not be motivated to modify Cai to include the fixed period length of Sakamoto as Cai describes a variable-length signal. Modification of the variable-length signal to be a fixed length signal would change the principle of the operation of Cai. "If the proposed modification or combination of the prior art would change the principle of operation of the prior art invention being modified, then the teachings of the references are not sufficient to render the claims prima facie obvious." MPEP 2143.01. Based on these distinctions, Applicants respectfully submit that Cai fails to disclose or suggest the limitations of claims 1, 8, and 9 missing from the other cited references.

The claims of the application are accordingly submitted to be in condition for allowance, and passage to issue is respectfully requested.
